prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Denver. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can give strong, practical next steps — and I can make a short list of named local practices if you tell me your Denver neighborhood or zip code. First, the quick answer to “which practices should I call” and why:

Which types of practices to call (and why)
- Board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS): best for complex extractions, bone grafting/sinus lifts, full-arch reconstructions, IV sedation, and surgical complications. They’re surgically focused and handle difficult cases.
- Board-certified periodontists who place implants: experts in gum/bone health and grafting; often good for single-tooth implants and complex bone/soft-tissue work.
- Prosthodontists or multidisciplinary implant centers: prosthodontists design and restore the implant crown/bridge/denture — important for esthetics and function. Multidisciplinary centers coordinate surgeon + restorative dentist for one streamlined plan.
- University dental clinic (University of Colorado Anschutz / CU School of Dental Medicine): lower-cost option; faculty-supervised residents can manage many implant cases, useful if cost is a factor.

How to find trustworthy local practices
- Use specialty directories: AAOMS (American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons) for OMS; American Academy of Periodontology (AAP) for periodontists; American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) for implant specialists. You can search by zip code.
- Check board certification: for oral surgeons check ABOMS board certification; for prosthodontists check ABO certification.
- Read recent patient reviews (Google, Healthgrades, Yelp) but weigh procedure-specific comments (implant outcomes) more than office décor.

What to look for / ask when you call (quick checklist)
- Do you place the implant and restore it, or do you coordinate with a restorative dentist? (Make sure both roles are clear.)
- How many implants of this type have you placed? How often do you do bone grafts/sinus lifts?
- Do you use CBCT 3D imaging and digital planning/guided surgery?
- What implant system(s) do you use (Nobel, Straumann, Zimmer, etc.)? Do you guarantee the implant or restoration?
- Sedation options and facility accreditation for sedation/IV?
- Expected timeline from extraction to final crown; approximate cost range and what’s included (doctor fees, surgery, grafting, temporary crown, final crown, follow-ups).
- Can you show before/after photos of similar cases and patient references?
- Is financing available / do you accept my insurance?

If you want specific names in Denver
Tell me:
- Your Denver neighborhood or zip code (e.g., Cherry Creek, Capitol Hill, North Denver, Downtown, Aurora),
- Whether you have dental insurance and any provider network needs,
- Whether you expect a simple single-tooth implant or anticipate grafts/full-arch work,
and I’ll compile 4–6 specific local practices (oral surgeons, periodontists, and a dental school option) with short reasons to call each.

Sample phone script you can use
“Hi, I’m calling because I need a dental implant for [single tooth/full-arch/extraction + implant]. Do you place implants? Do you do the surgical placement and/or the restoration? Do you use CBCT and digital planning? Can you give a ballpark cost and typical timeline for a case that requires [bone graft/no graft]? Do you accept [insurance name]? Thank you.”

If you want, give me your zip code and a short description of your situation (single tooth vs full-arch; insurance; urgency). I’ll return a concise list of specific Denver practices to call and why each is a good fit.
